prediction.likelyOutcome: This resolves in the jury's hands on a close, fact-intensive scope question: whether the Petco Site-Specific Work fell inside or outside the GMP. Brexton has a real but sub-50% chance of recovering something close to the ~$500,000 it claims, discounted heavily by the unconditional lien waivers it signed and the written Change Order requirement; Four Elyria's derivative fraud and slander of title claims are weaker standalone theories that largely track the same scope dispute and carry no independently quantifiable damages in this record. Net expected value favors a moderate, risk-adjusted recovery for Brexton well short of the full $500,000 ask, with meaningful odds of a wash or a modest net loss if the jury credits Four Elyria's scope theory and the lien waivers are read broadly.

issues.label: Core Scope Dispute: Site-Specific Work Inside or Outside the GMP
Four Elyria's Fraud Claim (Officers' Personal Liability)
Four Elyria's Slander of Title Claim

outcome.description: The trial court held the Site-Specific Work was outside the contract, granted summary judgment against Four Elyria on all its claims and for Brexton on unjust enrichment, and after a damages-only jury trial entered judgment for Brexton for $465,417.44; both sides' attorney-fee motions were denied and Brexton's lien-foreclosure counterclaim was dismissed. On this second appeal the court of appeals agreed the work was outside the contract but reversed in part and remanded for the trial court to apply the contract's Article 9 change-order provisions, leaving the unjust-enrichment award and the fee issues to be revisited on remand.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed in part and remanded; no final figure yet.
